subject: Sizing model and surge headroom for Stride Health committed TPS
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Lee <bethany@stridehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft capacity mapping and surge scenarios (attached)

Hi Bethany —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, I attached a small workbook that shows three traffic profiles you mentioned (steady, daily peak, and weekly marketing surge) and a first-pass mapping to dedicated GPU slabs. Key assumptions are inline in the file. High level:

- Target p95 generation latency: 250 ms for typical user flows (response length <= 512 tokens)
- Model family: customer-pref = open-70b quantized (q4_8-ish profile) for highest fidelity; we also show a lower-cost 13B variant for fallback/burst.
- Workload mix: ~65% short prompts (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128–512), 5% long (>512).

Attachment: stride_multiprong_traffic_estimates.csv — includes minute-by-minute sample day and a 10-min marketing surge window you called out.

Ask: can you confirm the weekly peak (you said ~09:00 ET on Tuesdays) and the maximum allowable p99 tail at ~800 ms? That will change the recommended headroom.

I’ve cc'd Marcus (solutions) to validate the slab math and Soojin on pricing.

— Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Bethany Lee <bethany@stridehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity mapping and surge scenarios (attached)

Connor —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the workbook. A few clarifications:

1) Weekly peak: yes — our campaigns typically create a 6–12 minute spike between 09:00–09:20 ET on Tuesdays. Peak concurrent requests historically lift ~3.5x over baseline, but tokens per request also grow (~+40%) because we append personalized context.
2) SLA fit: Our product team requires p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 900 ms for customers on our Silver plan (this is the target for the committed tier we are discussing).
3) Cost sensitivity: Procurement has asked for a committed slab count that keeps annual committed spend predictable, but we need a clear plan for burst breathing room without large temporary over-commitments.

Can Marcus confirm the GPU count required if we assume a 12-minute surge factor of 4x and want 25% headroom, while hitting p95 <= 300 ms on the 70B quantized profile? Also, what does fallback to a 13B variant look like (latency + cost)?

Happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

— Bethany
Dir, Product Operations
Stride Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity mapping and surge scenarios (attached)

Connor / team —

Quick sanity-check on the numbers from the workbook. I ran the per-GPU token/sec model against the provided mix. Key items:

- Assumptions used:
  * Model: open-70b q4_8 profile (inference path tuned for short/medium sequences)
  * Measured baseline throughput per A100-equivalent GPU (sustained, average request size ~160 tokens): ~3,200 tokens/sec.
  * For medium requests (~320 tokens) throughput drops to ~2,100 tokens/sec due to longer decode windows and KV footprint.
  * For burst/batched traffic we assume continuous batching with prefix caching for repeated prompts — effective uplift +18% on steady workloads.

- Baseline numbers from sheet (day-average): 1,800 tokens/sec sustained for Stride’s predicted mid-June weekday midday.

- Surge mapping (12-minute window at 4x requests and +40% tokens/request): peak token load ~12,500 tokens/sec.

Sizing recommendation (to meet p95 <= 300 ms with 25% headroom):
  * Production dedicated slabs for commit: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (sized for steady-state and day peaks) — provides ~12,800 tokens/sec effective with batching/caching uplift.
  * Headroom: that gives ~2.5–3x baseline vs average day and ~2.0x vs your expected 12-min surge after including cola-burst cost (we keep 25% headroom margin baked into the numbers).
  * But note: if peak profile includes many medium requests simultaneously (higher KV pressure), p95 moves up ~10–15% unless we add an extra GPU or partition those requests onto a mixed slab.

Fallback plan (cost / latency tradeoff):
  - 13B variant (quantized) per-GPU throughput: ~7,200 tokens/sec for short prompts, ~4,800 for mixed.
  - Recommendation: configure smart routing to fall back to 13B for marketing-surge traffic or low-risk cohorts. This reduces transient extra slabs by ~1–2 GPUs, cutting peak incremental spend by ~35% at the cost of model quality delta (we can A/B test for a specific cohort).

Open questions for Soojin / Neha on pricing and how much committed cushion procurement wants vs on-demand bursting. I’ll add a slide showing latency delta and estimated incremental monthly cost per extra GPU.

— Marcus
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Lee <bethany@stridehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@stridehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity mapping and surge scenarios (attached) — recommended path forward

Bethany / Procurement team —

Thanks for the details, Bethany. Summarizing the recommended, deal-aligned approach so Procurement has a clear option set:

Option A — Conservative commit (recommended for predictable spend + p95 SLO):
- Commit: 4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (Redwood Dedicated slab).
- Expected effective throughput: ~12.8k tokens/sec with caching/batching engaged.
- SLO: p95 <= 300 ms expected for your stated mix; p99 ~800–900 ms in worst-case medium-request pressure unless we add an extra GPU.
- Headroom: ~25% built-in; supports your 10–12 minute marketing surges with fallback routing to 13B for non-critical cohorts.
- Next steps: term sheet reflects commit, with 2 free burst credits per quarter and automatic on-demand bursting beyond commit at set overage rates.

Option B — Lower commit + smart fallback (lower spend, higher model risk):
- Commit: 2 GPUs, plus automated routing to 13B variant for surge windows.
- Effective peak coverage: covers ~60% of surge traffic on the high-fidelity model; remaining routed to 13B with expected p95 ~180–220 ms and lower quality.
- Good short-term for procurement that needs lower committed dollars.

Operational notes:
- We will instrument a per-minute token counter and a p95/p99 latency monitor in Console routed to your team.
- Suggest a 4-week ramp pilot: monitor two spikes and iterate routing thresholds.

Attachments: attached updated proposal (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf) with cost tables, and I’ve uploaded the annotated traffic CSV to the Drive link above.

If Procurement wants to lock a term today, Soojin can share a pricing sheet and finalize contract language. Happy to hop on a call this week to walk through the proposal.

Thanks —
Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
